The same models come back: a platinum blonde woman, a dark-haired woman, a young dark-haired man and an older grey-bearded man.

Row 4 is a second block in a volcanic and architectural setting: black lava rock (r4c4, r4c6) and dark angular concrete architecture (r4c2, r4c3), mixing B&W close portraits with colour three-quarter shots.

Row 3 is mostly an event block: a B&W press scrum (r3c1), a celebrity photocall in front of the logo backdrop (r3c2) and a night garden party at a glasshouse (r3c3). Two pencil sketch/craft tiles (r3c4, r3c6) sit either side of a B&W portrait (r3c5).

r2c4-r2c5 bring in warm summer presentation and backstage content (mannequins in a garden, embellished nude/ivory garments). These are the only clearly warm, saturated-leaning tiles and break up the cold campaign.
Wide and close shots alternate: landscapes and full-body figures (r1c5, r2c3, r1c1) are punctuated by tight B&W portraits (r1c4, r2c6, r3c5, r4c1, r4c5) roughly every 2-4 tiles.

Black-and-white is used for about a third of the tiles (r1c4, r2c6, r3c1, r3c5, r4c1, r4c2, r4c5). The rest are desaturated cool colour, apart from the warm event and backstage tiles (r2c4, r2c5, r3c3).
Formats are mixed: many carousels and reels, with only about 3 singles (r1c1, r1c2, r2c2, where no icon is visible). Reels are spread evenly through the grid rather than grouped.
Models almost never face the camera full on in wide shots; most look off to the side. Direct gaze is kept for close portraits and the frontal fur gilet shot.
Very few accessories: belts, ties, scarves and jewellery appear occasionally. No watches or bags are visible, and no branded cars or boats appear anywhere.
Row 4 tiles are cut off at the bottom by the screenshot (about 90% visible).
a.overall_style: Quiet luxury, editorial in feel. The cold palette is desaturated and close to monochrome: charcoal, ivory, taupe, grey-brown, with occasional burgundy. The wild northern landscapes are black volcanic beaches, glaciers and lava rock, and they serve as a minimalist backdrop for textured outerwear (shaggy furs, shearling, chunky mohair and boucle knits, tweed, wide trousers, shirt-and-tie layering). Fine-art B&W portraits with soft natural light are mixed in, along with brand-culture content: a celebrity photocall, garden presentations at night and by day, backstage details, and hand-drawn pencil sketches of the garments. Light is always soft and natural (overcast or diffuse), poses are calm and contemplative with averted gazes, and logos are almost absent apart from the event backdrop and the sketch label. Models span ages, with older grey-bearded men next to young women and men, and have diverse ethnicities.

b.overall_style: A quiet, editorial, nature-led luxury look. The palette is very restrained: charcoal, black volcanic sand, snow white, greige, taupe and cream, with rare accents in burgundy and oxblood. Light is overcast or diffused, and the colour grade is desaturated cool, with frequent true black-and-white and film-like grain. The models have a calm, unsmiling, contemplative presence. They often stand small in vast Icelandic-style landscapes or are shot in intimate close portraits. Wardrobe centres on texture: chunky knits, fur and shearling, wool tailoring, wide trousers, shirt-and-tie layering. Branding is nearly absent from campaign imagery. Logos appear only on event or craft tiles (photocall backdrop, sketch label). Visible accessories are minimal: no watches, sunglasses or bags on campaign models. Only a belt, ties, a neck scarf, and glasses and earrings on the backstage tile appear. No branded objects such as cars or boats are visible. Campaign storytelling is mixed with event coverage (night presentations, celebrity photocall) and craft or design-process content (pencil sketches), so the feed reads as a mood-driven magazine rather than a product catalogue. The age and gender cast is mixed and includes mature grey-haired men.

b.overall_style: Quiet-luxury, "old money" Italian menswear grid built around cream, grey, brown and black knitwear. grid_patterns: Rows 1-2 mix the autumn/winter tailoring campaign with the AC Milan partnership. The partnership tiles are r1c4 (logo wall), r1c6 (two men in pinstripe suits and crest ties on red), r2c1 (macro of the crest tie) and r2c2 (bearded man in front of the BOGGI MILANO/AC Milan wall). They form a red/black block that breaks the warm-neutral campaign images.
r1c1-r1c2 are one series: the same Venice canal shoot in grey/taupe/denim, first as a couple (carousel) and then as a group of five (reel).
r2c3-r2c4 look like one Trieste-like waterfront/piazza shoot in navy formalwear (navy double-breasted suit, navy overcoats).

Row 3 is mostly a coherent travel/commute series in navy, brown and burgundy. r3c1-r3c3 carry leather holdalls in a seafront piazza, outside a palazzo and on a staircase. r3c4 (bicycle) and r3c5 (quilted jacket reel) continue the navy/olive casual outerwear story.

Row 4 switches to a spring/summer sun campaign. It has saturated blue skies, sea, cliffs and sandstone, and a palette of ecru, beige, white, burgundy and rust (r4c1, r4c2, r4c5, r4c6), plus two street-style reels (r4c3, r4c4).
Framing alternates fairly often between wide/full-body (r3c1, r3c2, r3c3, r4c4) and waist-up or close shots (r1c3, r3c5, r4c1, r4c2). No row is all wide or all close.
Formats: mostly carousels with reels spread through the grid (r1c2, r1c4, r2c1, r3c2, r3c5, r4c3, r4c4). There is one single (r4c2). r2c2 and r3c3 have icons that cannot be read.
Colour grade runs by season: the top rows are muted-warm neutrals with red partnership accents, row 3 is natural/cool navy, and row 4 is saturated summer blue and ochre.
Logos are rare. They appear only on the partnership tiles and one reel overlay (r3c5). The campaign tiles carry no text.
a.overall_style: This reads as a polished commercial campaign feed for Italian smart-casual and formal menswear. Mostly young male models, sometimes with female models, are shot on location in Italian and European cities (Venice canals, a neoclassical piazza and courtyard, a library, an old-town brick street) and on Mediterranean coasts. Styling centres on double-breasted and unstructured blazers, knit polos, roll-necks, overshirts and quilted jackets. Accessories are frequent: sunglasses, leather holdalls/bags, ties, pocket squares, gloves, caps and a fedora. Light is natural daylight, soft in the city shoots and hard sun in the summer coastal ones. Every tile has a person except the logo wall and the tie macro. A recurring AC Milan official-tailoring partnership adds red/black logo content. Overall the feed is aspirational and travel-led, with a consistent neutral/navy palette that turns more saturated in the summer row.

b.brand_evidence: The BOGGI MILANO wordmark appears on a step-and-repeat wall with the AC Milan crest (r1c4), as a backdrop behind a footballer in a suit (r2c2), as a text overlay on r3c5, and woven as "BOGGI" under the AC Milan crest on a tie (r2c1). The AC Milan crest dated 1899 shows up on several tiles, which points to the Boggi x AC Milan official tailoring partnership. The rest of the grid is Italian-style menswear in the same look throughout: unstructured blazers, knit polos, tailored trousers and leather bags.

grid_patterns: The grid runs newest to oldest: Fall/Winter city tailoring on top, Spring/Summer coastal and Mediterranean at the bottom. The palette moves from greys and navy to beige, cream and burgundy as you go down.

There is an AC Milan partnership block of 4 tiles (r1c4, r1c6, r2c1, r2c2): a logo wall, players in pinstripe suits with red ties, a macro of the tie crest, and a footballer in front of the branded backdrop. They all use red and black with saturated studio or event light.
r1c1 and r1c2 come from the same canal-side shoot in grey, beige and denim tones, posted as a pair.
A Trieste-like square and palazzo series runs through r2c3, r2c4, r3c1 and r3c2: grand neoclassical squares, navy tailoring, leather holdalls.
Row 3 is a navy/black/burgundy smart-casual travel story: holdalls, a staircase, a bicycle and a quilted field jacket.
Row 4 is a summer coastal block: sky backdrops, rocky coast, sand cliffs and a beach hut. The palette is beige, cream, rust and burgundy, and the light is hard sun.

Wide and close shots alternate. Full-body or group shots (r1c2, r2c3, r3c1, r3c2, r3c3) sit next to tight portraits (r1c3, r3c5, r3c6, r4c1, r4c2). Every row has at least one close portrait and one full-length shot.
Formats are mostly carousels, with roughly one or two reels per row (r1c2, r1c4, r2c1, r3c2, r3c5, r4c3, r4c4). The r2c2 icon is unclear.

Almost every tile is a single male model. Women appear in r1c1, r1c2, r2c4, r4c1 and r4c4. Sunglasses and leather bags are the recurring accessories. Pocket squares and ties appear only in the formal tiles.
Branded text appears only in the AC Milan tiles and on r3c5. No cars or boats appear anywhere.
b.overall_style: Polished, commercial Italian menswear editorial. Most shots are on location, in heritage European cities (canals, neoclassical squares, palazzi, library interiors) and on Mediterranean coastlines. The colour grade is natural or warm, with saturated red studio work saved for the AC Milan partnership. The clothes are smart-casual tailoring: unstructured and double-breasted blazers, knit polos, roll-necks, overshirts and tailored trousers. Sunglasses and leather holdalls are the signature accessories. The models are young and aspirational, mostly men in their 20s. The grid mixes campaign wides, close portraits, partnership and logo content, and the occasional fabric detail. It reads as more accessible and lifestyle-led than quiet-luxury brands, and the football partnership gives it extra reach.
